subject: social_science

concepts.title: Primitive Subsistence Farming and Shifting Cultivation
concepts.definition: Traditional cultivation carried out on small plots using basic hand tools and family labor, heavily reliant on natural soil renewal and rainfall.
concepts.key_idea: Clearing forest patches for crop growth and relocating once land nutrients deplete.
question_patterns: in Class 10 geography: describe the features of primitive subsistence farming
explain how slash and burn agriculture works in traditional Indian farming
identify the regional names given to shifting cultivation across different Indian states
what are the main characteristics of slash and burn farming
contrast primitive subsistence farming with modern commercial agriculture

solution_steps.explain: Uses primitive tools like hoe, dao, digging sticks, and family or community labor.
Relies entirely on monsoons, natural soil fertility, and environmental suitability.
Farmers clear a fresh forest patch when soil fertility declines to allow natural soil replenishment.

concepts.title: Intensive Subsistence Farming
concepts.definition: High-density agricultural practice on smaller land holdings where heavy chemical inputs and manual labor are applied to maximize crop yields.
concepts.key_idea: High output extraction from divided land parcels caused by generational inheritance rights.
question_patterns: in Class 10 social science: detail the causes of high pressure on land in intensive subsistence farming
explain why landholdings become smaller across generations in India
what inputs are heavily utilized in intensive subsistence agricultural practices
analyze why farmers continue intensive farming on small plots despite low efficiency
outline the key features of intensive subsistence farming

solution_steps.explain: Practised in regions with dense population pressure on agricultural land.
Right of inheritance divides land across successive generations, making landholding sizes small.
Requires heavy doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation to obtain maximum yield from limited space.

concepts.title: Commercial Farming and Plantation Agriculture
concepts.definition: Agricultural production aimed primarily at market sales using high-yielding seeds, chemical agents, and capital-heavy plantation systems.
concepts.key_idea: Large-scale monoculture serving industrial production with integrated transport links.
question_patterns: in Class 10 geography: define plantation agriculture and state its chief characteristics
explain how modern inputs enhance productivity in commercial farming
identify major plantation crops grown in southern and north-eastern India
how does commercial farming bridge agriculture and industrial raw material supply
compare commercial farming practices between different Indian states

solution_steps.explain: Uses modern inputs like HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, insecticides, and pesticides for higher productivity.
Single crop grown over vast land tracts using capital-intensive methods and migrant labor.
All produce serves as raw material for processing industries, requiring good transport networks.

concepts.title: Cropping Seasons in India
concepts.definition: The division of the agricultural year into distinct sowing and harvesting cycles based on seasonal weather patterns and monsoon arrivals.
concepts.key_idea: Three annual cropping cycles known as Rabi, Kharif, and Zaid govern Indian crop schedules.
question_patterns: in Class 10 social science: differentiate between Rabi and Kharif cropping seasons
what is the Zaid season and which crops are harvested during this period
list the major crops sown during the winter Rabi season in northern India
explain the role of western temperate cyclones in supporting Rabi crop yield
identify the sowing and harvesting months for Kharif crops

solution_steps.explain: Sown in winter (October-December) and harvested in summer (April-June); crops include wheat, barley, peas.
Sown with monsoon onset and harvested in September-October; crops include paddy, maize, cotton.
Short summer season between Rabi and Kharif; produces watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and fodder crops.

concepts.title: Major Cereal Crops: Rice and Wheat
concepts.definition: The primary staple grain crops of India requiring distinct climatic conditions, rainfall levels, and geographical landscapes for growth.
concepts.key_idea: Rice thrives in warm humid monsoon zones while wheat requires cooler growing temperatures and bright sunshine during ripening.
question_patterns: in Class 10 geography: describe the geographical conditions needed for growing rice
what climate and soil conditions are required for optimal wheat cultivation
identify top rice and wheat producing states across India
explain how canal irrigation enabled paddy growth in dry north-western states
compare temperature and annual rainfall requirements for rice and wheat

solution_steps.explain: Kharif crop needing temperature above 25 deg C, high humidity, and annual rainfall above 100 cm.
Rabi crop requiring cool growing season, bright sunshine at ripening, and 50 to 75 cm annual rainfall.
Rice in northern and coastal plains/deltas; Wheat in Ganga-Satluj plains and Deccan black soil region.

concepts.title: Coarse Grains and Pulses
concepts.definition: Nutritious coarse grains adapted to dry climates alongside leguminous pulse crops that restore soil fertility.
concepts.key_idea: Coarse grains thrive in arid conditions while nitrogen-fixing pulses restore soil health in crop rotation systems.
question_patterns: in Class 10 social science: explain why pulses are vital in crop rotation
name the chief millet crops grown in India and highlight their nutritional value
which states are major producers of Jowar, Bajra, and Ragi
describe the soil and rainfall conditions necessary for growing Bajra and Ragi
identify why arhar differs from other pulse crops regarding soil fertility restoration

solution_steps.explain: Jowar, Bajra, and Ragi are coarse grains with high nutritional value (iron, calcium) suitable for dry/rain-fed areas.
Major vegetarian protein source surviving in dry conditions with low moisture requirements.
Leguminous nature enables pulses (except arhar) to fix atmospheric nitrogen and restore soil fertility.

concepts.title: Commercial Food Crops: Sugarcane, Oilseeds, Tea, and Coffee
concepts.definition: Non-grain cash crops grown for culinary, industrial, and beverage consumption under specific tropical and subtropical climates.
concepts.key_idea: Cash crops require substantial labor, moist frost-free weather, or tropical heat to yield commercial produce.
question_patterns: in Class 10 geography: outline climatic requirements for tea plantation growth
what conditions favour sugarcane cultivation and which states lead in its output
identify major oilseeds grown in India and their industrial uses
explain the significance of Arabica coffee variety cultivated in India
describe horticulture crops produced in various geographical zones of India

solution_steps.explain: Sugarcane needs hot humid climate (21 to 27 deg C, 75-100 cm rain); Oilseeds cover 12% cropped area as edible oil and industrial inputs.
Grows in deep, fertile, humus-rich soil; requires warm, moist frost-free climate with frequent showers and abundant labor.
Yemeni Arabica coffee grown on Baba Budan Hills; wide array of tropical/temperate fruits and vegetables produced.

concepts.title: Non-Food Crops: Rubber, Cotton, and Jute
concepts.definition: Industrial raw material crops including natural rubber and plant fibers cultivated under specific humidity and soil conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Fibre and rubber crops depend heavily on high rainfall, frost-free days, or fertile renewed floodplains.
question_patterns: in Class 10 social science: why is jute known as the golden fibre
describe the geographical conditions ideal for cotton cultivation
what climatic conditions are essential for growing natural rubber
identify major cotton and jute manufacturing states in India
explain the term sericulture and state how silk fibre is obtained

solution_steps.explain: Equatorial/tropical crop needing moist humid climate, over 200 cm rainfall, and temperature above 25 deg C.
Grows in Deccan black soil; requires high temperature, light rainfall/irrigation, 210 frost-free days, and bright sunshine.
Known as golden fibre; grows on renewed fertile floodplain soils under high growth temperatures.

concepts.title: Technological and Institutional Reforms in Indian Agriculture
concepts.definition: Government policies, modernization initiatives, and financial safeguards introduced to enhance agricultural productivity and farmer security.
concepts.key_idea: Land consolidation, Green Revolution, crop insurance, KCC, and MSP safeguard farming livelihoods against market and climate risks.
question_patterns: in Class 10 geography: list major institutional reforms introduced in Indian agriculture post independence
explain how Kisan Credit Card and PAIS support rural farmers
what is Minimum Support Price and how does it protect agriculturalists
describe the impact of Green Revolution and White Revolution on Indian farming
why were land consolidation and abolition of zamindari prioritized in early Five Year Plans

solution_steps.explain: Collectivisation, consolidation of holdings, cooperation, and abolition of zamindari prioritized in First Five Year Plan.
Green Revolution (package technology) and White Revolution (Operation Flood) introduced in 1960s-1970s.

solution_steps.action: List modern financial and support schemes
solution_steps.explain: Crop insurance, Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Personal Accident Insurance Scheme (PAIS), Grameen banks, and Minimum Support Price (MSP).

concepts.title: Bhoodan - Gramdan Movement
concepts.definition: A voluntary land-reform movement led by Vinoba Bhave involving non-violent donation of land to landless villagers, termed the Bloodless Revolution.
concepts.key_idea: Land donation by wealthy landowners to landless peasants facilitated social equity without state coercion.
question_patterns: in Class 10 social science: explain the origin and significance of Bhoodan Gramdan movement
who initiated the Bloodless Revolution in Indian agricultural history
describe Shri Ram Chandra Reddy's contribution to Pochampally land distribution
why did some landowners voluntarily donate land under the Gramdan movement
how did Vinoba Bhave carry forward Mahatma Gandhi's concept of Gram Swarajya

solution_steps.explain: Initiated by Vinoba Bhave, Mahatma Gandhi's spiritual heir, to spread the message of Gram Swarajya.
Shri Ram Chandra Reddy offered 80 acres of land to 80 landless villagers at Pochampally, starting Bhoodan.
Zamindars donated entire villages (Gramdan); voluntary non-violent land transfer earned the name Bloodless Revolution.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain the three cropping seasons of India with suitable crop examples for each.

solution_template.explain: Rabi crops are sown in winter (October to December) and harvested in summer (April to June). Key crops include wheat, barley, peas, gram, and mustard.
Kharif crops are sown at the onset of monsoon and harvested in September-October. Key crops include paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, and jute.
Zaid is a short summer cropping season between Rabi and Kharif. Key crops include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and fodder crops.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Enlist major institutional and technological reforms initiated by the Indian government to boost agricultural growth.

solution_template.explain: Land consolidation, collectivisation, cooperation, and abolition of zamindari were prioritized in the First Five Year Plan.
The Green Revolution and White Revolution (Operation Flood) introduced package technology and modern inputs in the 1960s and 1970s.
Provision of crop insurance, establishment of Grameen Banks, Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Personal Accident Insurance Scheme (PAIS), and Minimum Support Price (MSP).
